spiceReconnect.method: spice-gtk protocol client against the real installed Windows VM
spiceReconnect.evidence: After the client exited, a new client changed k to kk on the same VM. Repeated against the app-started VM: kk to kkk to kkkk.

appReconnect.settings: 50827 and SPICE enabled saved, app quit/relaunch preserved them. Out-of-range port rejected.
appReconnect.startup: Flutter release app started the existing VM with a new runtime socket and live connect buttons.
appReconnect.spice: App button launched spicy; terminating that viewer and clicking again produced a new four-channel connection without stopping QEMU.
appReconnect.ssh: User confirmed Windows command prompt after retry from the app SSH button. Independent verifier also authenticated twice against the app-started VM.
appReconnect.firstSshAttempt: Host-key fingerprint matched the previously verified guest key. Initial prompt ended with connection closed before password; retry succeeded. LoginGraceTime expiration is a possible explanation, not proven.

macosRelease.launchIsolation: Copied release build to a private validation app with a separate bundle identifier and ad-hoc signature; installed app untouched.

preservation.originalMediaEvidence: Not attached or written during this work; original ISO modification time predates this session. No initial full ISO hash was taken.
preservation.diskTPMNVRAM: Existing paths reused; cold APFS clone backup retained locally. Writable guest state legitimately changes during boot.

finalVMState: running; installed Windows desktop; app and SPICE viewer open
runtimeProbeCaveat: Early protocol tests used a native Swift harness. Final VM start, saved settings, live endpoints and viewer launch were exercised in the Flutter release app. SSH app authentication was user-confirmed; independent CLI evidence is recorded separately.

firewall.reason: Guest network is Public; installed rule originally applied only to Private.

viewerLimitations: GTK spicy accessibility requests timed out. Real screen/input was checked with the SPICE C protocol client; ordinary viewer launch/reconnect was checked by process and QMP channels. No claim of full GTK menu, clipboard, audio or USB redirection testing.
